content:
Apple is set to launch multiple new Macs later this year, including the first MacBook with a touch screen, the first computers powered by the M6 chip, and more. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming new Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be the first Mac ever to feature a touch screen. Whether the machine will be called the MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains undecided, but it will mark the most significant overhaul to the MacBook Pro in years.

Apple is reportedly testing these high-end MacBook models with macOS 27.1, a version that is likely to see an official release in late October.

This new MacBook will be Apple's first product to adopt both a touch screen and an OLED display. It is also expected to drop the notch design in favor of a Dynamic Island-style design similar to the iPhone. Bloomberg has also reported that the new high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touch screen MacBook will use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips found in the current MacBook Pro models.

M6 MacBook

Apple is reportedly planning to launch its first M6-powered Mac later this year. The company is working on a new base model MacBook Pro equipped with the next-generation M6 processor.

According to reports, the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth along with improvements in CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new base model MacBook Pro is not expected to see any other changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, bumping the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is now developing the next-generation update to the iMac, which is reportedly set to launch sometime this fall.

The new iMac is highly likely to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. Another rumor suggests that the new iMac will come with a fresh lineup of color options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (Possible Release)

Finally, Apple is also working on updates to the Mac mini and Mac Studio, but the release dates for these two machines remain uncertain.

As for the Mac mini, Apple is reportedly testing an all-new product line powered by M5 Pro and base M6 chips. Meanwhile, the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors.

According to Bloomberg, the release dates for these computers remain unclear, depending on "the supply situation of memory chips." The industry had widely expected the new Mac Studio to launch by the end of this year, but that now appears to be up in the air.

For reference, the current Mac mini is available with M4 and M4 Pro chips, while the Mac Studio comes in M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Affected by tight supply of memory and storage across the industry, Apple's Mac lineup is currently in a somewhat awkward position. However, the company still has a strong slate of new models waiting in the wings. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching by year-end? How much do you think the MacBook Ultra will be priced at? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
